newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended almost a cent weaker in listless trade ahead of a public holiday in South Africa on Friday, after busy two-way trade during the morning.
Bonds succumbed to similar lethargy with yields hardly moved from their weaker midday levels.
"Its been very, very quiet this afternoon which is typical before a long weekend," a currency trader said, adding that players had mostly been squaring positions after lunch.
South African markets will be closed for the Human Rights Day holiday on Friday.
The rand ended Thursday at 4.4335/4365 on the U.S. dollar from a 4.4260/4290 close on Wednesday.

Dealers said offshore dollar demand and steady local importer interest took the rand to its weakest level of 4.4445 bid during mid-morning dealings. But some strong exporter demand helped to take the unit off its lows.
Rumours of central Reserve Bank intervention at these top levels also abounded, but this could not be confirmed.
Dealers anticipated a range of 4.40-4.45 next week, another four-day week ahead of the Easter weekend.
"The guys may on Monday short it at first, selling dollars early and then buy them back later on," a dealer said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.0760/0862 on sterling from 7.0781/0873 at the close on Wednesday and at 0.3782/3786 marks from 0.3796/3800 previously.
On the bond market the key R150 bond was trading at 15.17 percent at 1410 GMT, over ten basis points higher from 15.055 at the same time on Wednesday.
Dealers said although trade was quiet in the afternoon, players had kept an eye on weaker U.S. Treasuries.

The key 30-year U.S. bond had attempted to push through the seven percent level several times on Wednesday amid concerns about a hike in interest rates following the release of mildly inflationary CPI data.
"There is some upward pressure on the U.S. bond and our guys are very aware of it," a dealer said.
They said attention would be focused on Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on the U.S. economy later for any sign of a move in interest rates.
Dealers said South African bonds yields were seen heading higher next week under pressure from the U.S. market and if the rand continued its weaker trend.
"We are busy with a smallish bear market here and it is likely to continue next week," another trader said.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners sold a net 317.59 million rand's worth of bonds on Wednesday after selling 129.05 million on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market amounted to 7.59 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.13 billion rand on Tuesday.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage once again rose above the 10 billion rand level touching 10.068 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.918 billion on Tuesday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
